analysis: What changed versus Wednesday's 9:00 AM brief: the story flipped overnight. Wednesday's rally (S&P 500 +1.31% to 7,619.38, Nasdaq +1.60%) was built on CoreWeave's earnings answering the AI-credit question — and the overnight Nvidia leadership crisis has put that answer back in doubt. The WSJ reported Wednesday evening that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang after the NYT reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with an Nvidia executive who reports to him; Bloomberg added the board is working with an outside firm on successors and weighing an interim CEO. No decision has been announced and news is expected later Thursday, so the -7% premarket move prices uncertainty, not a done deal — but the governance overhang from Wednesday (House briefing deadline, subpoena threat) has escalated into a succession question at the company at the center of the AI trade, with no named successor and Huang on record as not believing in succession planning. The rotation inside chips is the tell: AMD and Broadcom are up 3%+ premarket while NVDA, CoreWeave (-7.2% after +24.7%), Micron and Sandisk fall — the market is redistributing AI exposure rather than abandoning it outright, which matches Saxo's framing of the key question. The other half of Wednesday's rally, rates, is unresolved: the 10Y is back near 5.00% with the bond market reopened after Veterans Day, a December hike is priced at 100% after the hot October CPI, and five Fed speakers are on today's docket. Signal vs noise: the board deliberation (multi-outlet, sourced to people familiar) and the premarket repricing are signal; the '20% further drop if Huang departs' analyst warnings are scenario talk, not a forecast; the Anthropic IPO demand story remains a sentiment tailwind but is secondary today. The HN circular-financing thread is the useful counterweight to Wednesday's celebration — the funding-structure questions CoreWeave's prepayments answered for one name are now being asked of the whole complex again.

community_signals.takeaway: 182-comment thread dissecting the circular financing behind the GPU boom (Nvidia, CoreWeave, Nebius) — the funding-structure skepticism that Wednesday's CoreWeave print briefly answered and that today's Nvidia leadership shock puts back on the table.
community_signals.title: Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius: Inside the Circular Financing of the GPU Boom

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 7% in premarket trading Thursday after the Wall Street Journal reported its board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, following the New York Times' report of a second extramarital relationship — this one with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's VP of healthcare, who reports directly to him. The board met Wednesday night; Bloomberg reported it is working with an outside firm on possible successors and weighing an interim CEO. No decision has been announced, with news expected later Thursday. The first affair, with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom U.S. intelligence officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence, was acknowledged by Huang on Sunday; the board opened an independent investigation (Wachtell Lipton, led by former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim) and said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. The House briefing deadline passed Wednesday with no public reply from Huang, and subpoena threats stand. NVDA closed Wednesday at $173.73 (+2.87%). NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17. Last reported quarter (Q2 FY2027, Aug 26): EPS $2.22 vs $2.09 consensus, revenue $96.22B.
headlines.why_it_matters: A succession question at the company at the center of the AI trade, with no named successor — the -7% move prices uncertainty, not a done deal, so any board statement later today is the swing factor for the whole complex.

headlines.why_it_matters: Wednesday's CoreWeave-led rally is giving back its tech half overnight while the Dow holds flat — the classic rotation shape, with the Nvidia headline doing the damage rather than broad selling.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave (CRWV) fell about 7.2% in premarket trading after surging 24.71% on Wednesday on its Q3 beat and raised outlook ($132.5B backlog, ~$9B of customer prepayments expected within three months). The chip complex is split: AMD and Broadcom each gained over 3% premarket, while Intel, Sandisk, Micron, Dell, Marvell, TSMC, Oracle and Palantir fell; ASML dropped over 3% in Europe and SoftBank slid over 3% in Tokyo. The Stoxx 600 rose 0.3% to a record high on rotation away from AI.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade is redistributing, not collapsing — money is moving toward AMD/Broadcom and non-AI names while the Nvidia-linked names take the hit, so breadth within chips matters more than the index level today.

headlines.why_it_matters: Outside Nvidia, the megacaps are mostly flat premarket — the overnight damage is concentrated in the AI-infrastructure names, not a broad megacap selloff.

headlines.headline: Rates are back in focus as the bond market reopens after Veterans Day: the 10-year Treasury yield is nudging higher to trade close to 5.00%. A December Fed hike is priced at 100% (86.2% for 25bp) after October headline CPI came in hot (+0.4% MoM vs +0.3% expected, core +0.3% vs +0.2%), and Goldman now expects another hike in March 2027. Five Fed speakers are on today's docket, including New York Fed President John Williams, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Governor Michael Barr. Today's data: weekly jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET (expected 195,000 vs 189,000 last week) and October existing home sales at 10:00 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: Equities rallied Wednesday into a rates vacuum; Thursday is the first live read on whether the bond market accepts the bounce at a 5% 10-year with a hike fully priced.

headlines.headline: Earnings today: Nebius (NBIS) reports before the open; after the close, Cisco (EPS est. $1.33, options imply ±7.9%) and Applied Materials (EPS est. $4.06, options imply ±7.5%) — both are tests of AI infrastructure spending. Friday brings October PPI at 8:30 AM ET. Anthropic's IPO roadshow continues to draw strong demand, with a reported ~$1.4T fully diluted valuation target; pricing expected Nov 18, first trading Nov 19 (per CNBC, unconfirmed dates). Kenvue delists today ahead of the Kimberly-Clark close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cisco and Applied Materials after the close are the next fundamental check on AI spending — if they disappoint, the Nvidia-driven doubt hardens into a demand question.

headlines.headline: Oil eased overnight: WTI about $85.8 (-0.9%) and Brent about $91.9 (-0.9%) in early Thursday trade, though Brent later recovered to just below $93 (+0.2%) per Dow Jones. No new Hormuz incident was reported; the UKMTO-confirmed tanker strike northeast of Lima, Oman, stands, while reports of a tanker hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz remain unverified. Gold fell back below $4,000 an ounce and Bitcoin traded lower around $73,500.
headlines.why_it_matters: The supply-risk premium is easing slightly even as equities wobble — oil is not amplifying today's move, and gold slipping below $4,000 cuts against a flight-to-safety read.
